note: Literature consistently documents pituitary hypoplasia/aplasia or hypopituitarism across reported TBC1D32-related ciliopathy/Alsahan-Harris cases, making complete penetrance of structural anomalies plausible to investigate.

evidence.text: Previously reported probands with TBC1D32 recessive disease consistently show absence or hypoplasia of the pituitary gland, pointing to critical TBC1D32 involvement in hypothalamic-pituitary development.

source.title: Diagnosis of TBC1D32‐associated conditions: Expanding the phenotypic spectrum of a complex ciliopathy
source.quote: reported probands had absence/hypoplasia of the pituitary

evidence.text: Brain MRI in TBC1D32 ciliopathy patients revealed pituitary hypoplasia, with literature review reinforcing hypopituitarism and pituitary structural defects as hallmark manifestations of the disorder.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and molecular spectrum of TBC1D32-related ciliopathy: case reports and literature Review
